# Jordan Nationwide 5G SA Network – Nominal Design Report

**Scope:** coverage, capacity, antenna/sector plan, frequency plan, fiber transport, 5G core and indoor coverage for a greenfield 5G Standalone network covering Jordan, with a **1 Gbps single-user downlink target in urban and suburban areas**.
**Status:** nominal (pre-survey) design. Generated by `tools/generate_design.py`; every number below is reproducible and changes when the inputs at the top of that script change.

| Deliverable | File |
|---|---|
| Interactive satellite map (coverage, sites, sectors, fiber, indoor) | `index.html` (run `python -m http.server 8765` in this folder → http://localhost:8765) |
| Site list (6,270 sites: position, ground elevation, building height, antenna height, backhaul, hub, ring) | `output/sites.csv` |
| Cell list (18,675 sectors: azimuth, mechanical / digital / RET tilts, PCI, border flag) | `output/sectors.csv` |
| Fiber rings, hubs, indoor venues | `output/fiber_rings.csv`, `output/hubs.csv`, `output/indoor_venues.csv` |
| All KPIs, link budgets, compliance statistics | `output/summary.json` |

### What “1 Gbps guaranteed when a user uses it” means in this design
A user who is alone on the air interface of a sector receives the whole carrier. His rate is then set only by bandwidth and SINR:

`rate = BW × 0.74 (TDD DL share) × 0.86 (1 − overhead) × rank-adaptive spectral efficiency (≤ 4 layers, 256-QAM, 0.7 × Shannon)`

→ 1 Gbps needs SINR ≈ **13.9 dB with 300 MHz**, 17.7 dB with 200 MHz, 27.4 dB with 100 MHz.
The grid is interference-limited (noise is irrelevant outdoors), so SINR is fixed by **neighbour-cell load**, not by power. The design therefore (a) gives every 1 Gbps sector 3 × 100 MHz of n78, and (b) dimensions the grid so busy-hour load stays ≈ 4–11 %, where ≥ 95 % of locations reach 1 Gbps. Processor-sharing view: at 11 % load a user finds the sector idle ≈ 89 % of the time; when two users collide, MU-MIMO (64T64R, up to 16 layers) still serves both near 1 Gbps in mid-cell. **Expansion trigger:** busy-hour PRB utilisation > 20 % on a sector → add n258 layer or split. The residual 2–5 % of locations (deep wadis, cell corners) are covered by n258 hotspots, C-RAN coordinated scheduling / DL CoMP, or fall back to ≥ 700 Mbps.

Honest limits: this is a **median** prediction; deep indoor behind Jordanian stone façades reaches 1 Gbps in only 50–90 % of locations from the macro layer – that is why large buildings get dedicated indoor systems (§8) and homes are served by window/outdoor FWA CPE.

## 2. Inputs and method

| Input | Source | Use |
|---|---|---|
| Terrain | **Copernicus GLO-90 DEM** (ESA, 3″) – 29 tiles mosaicked | site ground elevation; nominals moved to the local high point in their search ring (4,806 sites moved, mean gain 17 m); per-sector terrain-aware tilt; knife-edge diffraction (ITU-R P.526) along every site→pixel profile; true 3-D antenna geometry in predictions; Dead Sea water mask |
| Building heights | **GHSL GHS-BUILT-H R2023A** (EU JRC, 100 m average net building height, epoch 2018) | antenna height = max roof within 250 m + 8 m clearance; rooftop vs monopole decision; 311 nominals deleted because their whole cell contains no buildings; verification of clutter classes |
| Borders / governorates | geoBoundaries ADM0 / ADM1 | clipping, border-sector handling, statistics |
| Satellite imagery | Esri World Imagery (map backdrop) | digitising built-up zones, visual verification |
| Propagation | 3GPP TR 38.901 UMa-NLOS (city), RMa-NLOS (rural) with LOS floor, + DEM diffraction | coverage / SINR / throughput rasters at 50 m (n78) and 300 m (n28) |

Measured clutter statistics (GHSL at site locations): DU mean building 14.5 m (p95 27.7 m); U 8.1 m (p95 18.8 m); SU 3.5 m (p95 12.9 m).

Not yet included (needed before build): 3-D building vectors / 2 m clutter for ray-based prediction in DU, CW drive-test model calibration, candidate-site acquisition, structural surveys.

Spectrum actually held is an **assumption**. Public sources confirm only that TRC assigned parts of 3400–3800 MHz to Zain, Orange and Umniah for 5G (2022–23); per-operator amounts, 700 MHz and 26 GHz availability must be confirmed with TRC. A 300 MHz n78 holding implies a single wholesale / shared-RAN network or spectrum pooling.

## 3. Frequency plan

| Band | Spectrum | Duplex | Radio | Role |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| n28 (700 MHz) | 2 × 10 MHz | FDD | 2T4R city / 4T4R rural | National coverage layer, deep indoor, VoNR, UL anchor – on every site |
| n3 (1800 MHz) | 2 × 20 MHz | FDD | 4T4R | PCell + uplink for FDD-TDD CA (UL/DL decoupling), rural capacity |
| n1 (2100 MHz) | 2 × 15 MHz | FDD | 4T4R | Additional FDD capacity (DU, U, rural) |
| **n78 (3400–3700 MHz)** | **3 × 100 MHz** | TDD | **64T64R** (8T8R rural) | **1 Gbps layer**, reuse 1, 3-CC DL CA |
| n258 (26 GHz) | 800 MHz (4 × 200) | TDD | street / indoor heads | DU hotspots, venues, FWA |

* TDD frame: DDDSU, 30 kHz SCS, special slot 10:2:2, phase-synchronised nationally (±1.5 µs) and coordinated with neighbouring-country 3.5 GHz networks and any legacy LTE-TDD in 3.5 GHz (fallback frame DDDDDDDSUU if required).
* 3700–3800 MHz left as guard / FSS earth-station protection and future 4th carrier.
* Carrier aggregation set: n3 (PCell, UL) + n1 + n78 × 3 → ≈ 335 MHz DL. UL on n78 where RSRP allows, otherwise on n3/n1.
* PCI: 336 groups × 3, greedy assignment with reuse distance ≥ 6 × ISD, mod-3 distinct within a site (values in `sectors.csv`). SSB: 8 beams (Case C) on carrier 1. PRACH: format B4 in cities, format 0 (14.5 km) rural/highway. TAC per hub cluster (~40 sites).

| Urban (U) | Amman, Zarqa, Russeifa, Irbid, Aqaba, Salt, Madaba, Mafraq, Jerash, Ajloun, Karak, Tafilah, Ma'an, Ramtha, Wadi Musa, Baqa'a – 534 km² | 450 m | 300 m | 30–36 m | 3 | as DU without n258 |
| Suburban (SU) | outskirts of all the above, QAIA, Dead Sea hotel strip, Aqaba south coast/ASEZA, Jordan-Valley towns, Azraq, Mutah – 959 km² | 650 m | 433 m | 32–38 m | 3 | n78 64T64R 3×100 MHz + n3 4T4R + n28 2T4R |
| Rural populated | NW highlands and Karak–Tafilah plateau – 8,800 km² | 4.5 km | 3 km | 45 m tower | 3 | n28 4T4R + n1/n3 4T4R + n78 8T8R |
| Highway / desert | 15 routes, ≈ 2,000 km | 7 km | 5 km | 45 m tower | 2 (along road) | n28 4T4R + n3 4T4R |

### 4.1 Antenna system (per sector)
1. **n78 AAU** – 64T64R, 192 elements, 320 W, 400 MHz IBW; traffic-beam gain 24 dBi (SSB 20 dBi); horizontal scan ±60°; vertical HPBW ≈ 6°, digital tilt −2…+9°; ≈ 0.5 m², < 30 kg.
2. **Passive multiband antenna** 2L4H, 2.0 m (2.6 m rural): 2 ports 698–960 MHz (15.5 dBi, V-HPBW 9°) + 4 ports 1695–2690 MHz (17.5 dBi, V-HPBW 5.5°), independent RET 2–12° per band group; fed by n28 and n1/n3 RRUs mounted behind the antenna (jumper loss ≤ 0.5 dB).
3. DU hotspots: n258 radios on street furniture at 8–10 m, 120–150 m apart.

### 4.2 Sectorisation and azimuth
* **3 sectors per macro site, azimuths 30° / 150° / 270°** on a hexagonal lattice (3GPP layout: each boresight points at a neighbour site’s back-to-back null; ISD = 1.5 × cell range). All city sites share the pattern so the grid stays regular after the terrain micro-move.
* **Highway sites: 2 sectors** aligned with the local road bearing (per-site values in `sectors.csv`).
* Rural/highway sectors whose footprint lies outside Jordan (border, Dead Sea, Gulf of Aqaba) are **removed**. City sectors whose boresight crosses a border or the sea within 2 km are kept, get **+2° tilt**, and are flagged for cross-border coordination: **109 sectors** (Aqaba–Eilat/Taba, Jordan Valley, Ramtha–Daraa, Dead Sea shore).
* Detailed planning should rotate individual sites ±20° to align with street canyons / avoid pointing along wadis; the regular plan is the starting point.

### 4.3 Tilt (terrain-aware, per sector)
`total tilt = atan( (h_ant + z_site − z̄_footprint − 1.5 m) / cell range ) + V-HPBW/2`, clamped to 2–14°.
z̄_footprint = mean DEM height of 9 points at 0.5 / 0.75 / 1.0 × range and −30° / 0° / +30° off boresight.
n78 takes up to 9° digitally; any remainder is mechanical (shared bracket), and mid-/low-band RETs are then set independently.

| Class | Mean total n78 tilt | 10th–90th percentile | Flat-terrain value |
|---|---|---|---|
| DU | 9.6° | 7–14° | 8.4° |
| U | 9.2° | 6–13° | 8.4° |
| SU | 8.1° | 5–12° | 7.0° |
| Rural (low band) | 4.6° | 3–7° | 5.3° |
| Highway (low band) | 3.6° | 3–4° | 5.0° |

The wide spread in Amman (hilltop sites looking into wadis need 12–14°, valley sites looking uphill 2–5°) is exactly why tilts must be terrain-driven. 1,190 sectors hit the 14° clamp – candidates for lower mounting height or site relocation in detailed design.

### 4.4 Antenna height (building-aware)
`h_ant = max(class default, max GHSL height within 250 m + 8 m)`, capped at 60 m. Rooftop if local buildings ≥ 9 m, else monopole. Result: 2,652 rooftops, 3,040 monopoles/greenfield, 578 lattice towers. GHSL is a 100 m average, so individual towers (Abdali, Jordan Gate, hotel towers) exceed it – these are handled by the indoor programme and by choosing the tallest roof in the search ring at acquisition.

## 6. Capacity and 1 Gbps compliance

**Traffic model (design year):** 40 % of the population on this network (4.2 M subs), 80 GB/sub/month, 10 % of the day’s traffic in the busy hour → 0.59 Mbps/sub, ≈ 2.5 Tbps nationally. Mean cell spectral efficiency 10 b/s/Hz (64T64R MU-MIMO), 4 b/s/Hz for rural 8T8R.

| Class | Pop. density | Subs / sector | Offered BH Mbps / sector | Load @100 MHz | @200 MHz | **@300 MHz** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DU | 25,000 /km² | 407 | 241 | 32.6 % | 16.3 % | **10.9 %** |
| U | 10,000 /km² | 240 | 142 | 19.2 % | 9.6 % | **6.4 %** |
| SU | 2,500 /km² | 142 | 84 | 11.4 % | 5.7 % | **3.8 %** |
| Rural | 150 /km² | 396 | 235 | 57.5 % | 33.3 % | 23.5 % |

**Terrain-aware compliance – % of 50 m pixels with single-user DL ≥ 1 Gbps (n78 + 35 MHz FDD CA), outdoor:**

| Neighbour load | DU 100 / 200 / 300 MHz | U 100 / 200 / 300 MHz | SU 100 / 200 / 300 MHz |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10 % (design busy hour) | 25 / 77 / **97.9** | 28 / 79 / **97.6** | 33 / 78 / **95.5** |
| 20 % (expansion trigger) | 11 / 51 / 78 | 14 / 54 / 80 | 18 / 55 / 80 |
| 30 % | 6 / 37 / 62 | 8 / 40 / 65 | 12 / 44 / 66 |
| 50 % | 2 / 22 / 44 | 3 / 25 / 47 | 6 / 30 / 50 |

At the design point (300 MHz, 10 %): in-car/light indoor 97.5 / 96.5 / 88.2 %; deep indoor 90.4 / 82.8 / 50.4 %. SS-RSRP ≥ −105 dBm over 100 / 99 / 96 % of DU / U / SU area.

**Conclusions**
1. The site grid is sufficient; **bandwidth and load control deliver the guarantee**. 100 MHz cannot do it at any density.
2. Keep busy-hour load under ≈ 15 %: QoS flow with GFBR for the 1 Gbps tariff, fair-use shaping of bulk traffic, n258 offload where utilisation > 20 %.
3. C-RAN in DU/U (§7) enables coordinated beamforming / CoMP, worth ≈ 3–5 dB at cell edges – the margin that lifts the last 2–5 % of pixels.

## 7. Transport, fiber and core

**RAN architecture.** DU/U: **C-RAN** – AAUs connect by eCPRI (7-2x), 3 × 25GE per AAU over dark fiber (≤ 10 km, ≤ 75 µs) to DU hotels co-located with the 150 hubs. SU/rural: D-RAN with DU at site, 25GE backhaul.

| Tier | Topology | Capacity | Fiber |
|---|---|---|---|
| Access | 849 rings, ≤ 8 sites, dual-homed to hub; ring geometry generated per hub (angular sectors, out-and-back) | 25GE (50GE-ready); site peak = 5.2 Gbps sector peak + mean of other sectors ≈ 8 Gbps | 48-core, 5,737 km route (street factor 1.35); 12-core site drop |
| Aggregation | 41 rings of ≤ 5 hubs to a PoP | 100GE, SRv6 + EVPN, FlexE hard slices | 96-core, 887 km |
| Metro core | Amman ring DC1 – North – Zarqa – DC2 – South – DC1, Centre PoP dual-homed | N × 400GE | 87 km |
| Backbone | **Southern national ring:** Amman – Desert Highway – Ma'an – Aqaba – Wadi Araba – Dead Sea – Amman. **Northern ring:** Amman – Zarqa – Mafraq – Ramtha – Irbid – Jerash – Amman. Regional spurs: King's Highway (Madaba–Karak–Tafilah–Petra–Ma'an), Jordan Valley, Salt–Deir Alla, Ajloun, Karak–Qatraneh, Tafilah–Jurf, Azraq, Safawi–Ruwaished, Wadi Rum | DWDM/OTN N × 400G (national), 100G (regional) | 1,979 km; doubles as highway-site backhaul (add/drop ≤ 2 km, 201 km of spurs) |
| Rural off-route | 360 sites | E-band 10G ≤ 6 km, else 6–18 GHz XPIC | – |

**Synchronisation:** GNSS + ePRTC at DCs/PoPs, PTP G.8275.1 with full on-path support and SyncE; ±1.5 µs network-wide, ±130 ns inside C-RAN clusters for CA/CoMP; GNSS at every hub as backup.

**5G core (SA, cloud-native, 3GPP Rel-17):** AMF, SMF, AUSF, UDM/UDR, PCF, NRF, NSSF, NEF, SCP, BSF, CHF and IMS (VoNR – there is no LTE fallback in a pure-SA network, so VoNR on n28/n3 is mandatory from day 1) active-active in **DC1 Amman West** and **DC2 Amman East**; UDR replica / DR in Irbid. **Distributed UPF + MEC + CDN:** DC1/DC2 ≈ 55 %, Amman Centre + Zarqa 15 %, Irbid 15 %, Aqaba 8 % (also international gateway at the submarine-cable landing), remainder regional. N+1 UPF pools sized for 2.5 Tbps. Slices: eMBB-1G (GFBR), FWA, enterprise/private, public safety, O&M.

## 8. Indoor coverage (malls, hotels, airports, hospitals, campuses)

Macro n78 loses 20–30 dB through Jordanian stone/concrete façades, so every large building gets a dedicated **digital indoor system** (passive DAS cannot carry 4×4 MIMO at 3.5 GHz economically).

| Venue type | Design rule | Example result |
|---|---|---|
| Mall / mixed-use | n78 4T4R pRRU (3×100 MHz, 4 × 250 mW) per ≈ 550 m² of public area, 20–25 m grid, CAT6A/hybrid-fiber to RHUB (8 pRRU each); n258 heads in atria and food courts | Abdali Mall 248 pRRU + 10 mmW; Mecca Mall 208; City Mall 175 |
| Hotel / resort | 1 pRRU per ≈ 5 rooms (corridor-mounted), + public areas per 500 m², ballroom/lobby mmWave | Amman Rotana 125 pRRU; Tala Bay cluster 252 |
| Airport / convention | per 600 m² + mmWave at gates, check-in, halls | QAIA 172 pRRU + 13 mmW |
| Hospital / campus | per 650 m² of served floor, EMC review in clinical areas | University of Jordan 270 |
| Stadium | n78 + n258 narrow-beam bowl sectors (≈ 1 per 700 seats) | Amman Intl Stadium 24 mmW sectors |

Indoor budget: 24 dBm/port, InH-NLOS 76 dB at 15 m → RSRP ≈ −85 dBm, SINR > 25 dB, rank 4 → 1.5–3 Gbps per user. Dedicated PCIs, reduced SSB power at entrances, 3 dB HO offset to stop leakage; each venue dual-fiber homed (2 × 10GE, 2 × 25GE above 60 pRRUs) to the nearest hub; in-building DU. Total for the 51 listed venues (Amman, Dead Sea, Aqaba, Petra, Irbid): ≈ 5,340 pRRUs, 196 mmWave heads. Venue coordinates and areas are approximate – confirm by survey; phase 2 adds every building > 10,000 m² or > 8 floors.

## 10. Risks and next steps
1. **Spectrum** – secure 3 × 100 MHz n78 (or accept ≈ 78 % compliance with 200 MHz and fill with n258). Confirm 700 MHz and 26 GHz availability with TRC.
2. **Model calibration** – CW measurements in Amman (hills + stone clutter), Irbid, Aqaba; replace UMa with a tuned SPM/ray model on 2–5 m building data for DU.
3. **Site acquisition** – 6,270 nominals with 0.2 × ISD search rings; reuse of existing operator towers/rooftops should be maximised (sharing can cut new builds by > 50 %).
4. **Cross-border coordination** – 109 flagged sectors; TDD frame alignment with neighbours.
5. **Phasing** – P1 Amman–Zarqa–Irbid–Aqaba DU/U + backbone (≈ 3,400 sites); P2 suburban + governorate capitals; P3 rural/highway + indoor phase 2.
6. **Device ecosystem** – 1 Gbps needs UEs supporting n78 3-CC DL CA (300 MHz) with 4 Rx; verify the target handset/CPE portfolio.
